scope: Replay the six actual native VideoEncoder input frames captured from the production SceneExporter. Standalone Chromium 151.0.7922.34 WebCodecs plus independent FFmpeg 6.0 decode; not installed Electron or full-song acceptance.

lockedInputs.invariants: No material, noise, dimensions, frame ordering, timing or original decoded-interior RGB MAE < 3 gate changes. The original baseline encode options remain fixed; each diagnostic variant declares its changed fields. Six captured native inputs equal the independent CPU oracle byte-for-byte. Observed and unobserved production outputs have identical encoded and decoded hashes.

singleFactors.result: Original packet payloads and full decoded RGB reproduced. Explicit latency quality/realtime and variable bitrate mode reproduce the same packets. Constant bitrate changes packets but fails. 560000 bps improves late frames but still fails all six gates; this early isolated bitrate factor retained the original level-10 string and is not production level-conformance evidence.

shortProfileRejection.result: Both short profile-1 cases were rejected by capability queries. No fallback occurred and no profile-1 result was claimed. Original and level-only P0 controls reproduced the original packets/RGB.

matchedFullCodecMatrix.controls: Original short P0 level-10, short P0 level-30 and full P0 level-30 explicit-default low-budget cases all reproduce every original VP9 packet payload and full FFmpeg RGB bytes. IVF framing is independently checked against every native packet SHA256.

codecGrammar.shortProfile1Rejection: Omitted optional fields default to 4:2:0, incompatible with profile 1. The optional chroma/color group is all-or-none. P0 supports 4:2:0; P1 supports 4:2:2 or 4:4:4.
codecGrammar.controlledFields: Every factorial cell uses level 30 and identical primaries/transfer/matrix/range declarations. The chroma factor legally changes profile and subsampling together, not just one profile byte. All four paired comparisons assert that no other actual configure field changes.
codecGrammar.actualColorMetadata: FFprobe and Chromium decoder configuration report smpte170m limited-range YUV, not the BT.709 color declaration in the requested codec string. Requested fields are not accepted as proof of actual encoded color metadata.

established: This failure is downstream of correct native encoder inputs, not application frame ordering, canvas reuse or a wrong scene clock.
The bitrate target and legal chroma/profile mode both influence error, but neither tested high-bitrate profile passes the unchanged gate.
Chromium and FFmpeg independently reproduce the fidelity loss, so it is not an FFmpeg-only decoder defect.
Codec level and explicit optional defaults were isolated and did not change this baseline's packet payloads.
notEstablished: The exact division between RGB/YUV conversion, subsampling and VP9 quantization residuals.
A mathematical impossibility result for every possible 4:2:0 encoder or a universally sufficient bitrate.
A production fix, final export-quality policy or installed Electron/full-song acceptance.

productionGuidance: Keep compatible 4:2:0 output explicitly lossy; do not promise per-frame RGB fidelity or silently change the existing profile.

Current production very_high 4:4:4 at 93000 bps failed this fixture; even the isolated 5600000-bps matched 4:4:4 configuration still fails. No sufficient bitrate or safe global multiplier was demonstrated.

A high-fidelity/master preset needs validated quality control or an explicit lossless/intermediate route, with clear capability failure. A bitrate label alone must not advertise fidelity that the decoded artifact does not meet.
Retain the original failing gate and artifacts. Any eventual policy change needs representative resolution/frame-rate/content coverage, not this one tiny fixture alone.

nextReadOnlyDiagnosticDesign.inputRule: Use only the existing locked BGRA bytes and already encoded payloads. Do not regenerate noise, re-time frames, alter content or relax RGB acceptance.
nextReadOnlyDiagnosticDesign.decoderPlaneControl: Decode retained VP9 packets to native YUV planes via Chromium VideoFrame.copyTo without RGB conversion, and extract the same native pixel format through FFmpeg without resampling. Compare plane bytes, layouts, strides and timestamps before any RGB readback.
nextReadOnlyDiagnosticDesign.noCodecRoundtrip: In a private artifact directory, convert the locked BGRA frames to explicit limited-range BT.601 YUV444 and back to RGB without an encoder. Repeat 4:2:0 separately with the chosen chroma resampling flags recorded. Compare every original RGB frame using the same interior gate.
nextReadOnlyDiagnosticDesign.encodedPlaneComparison: Compare actual decoded Y/U/V planes with the no-codec forward-conversion planes. First establish equal native-decoder planes; then report conversion-only RGB residual separately from encoded-plane residual.
nextReadOnlyDiagnosticDesign.limits: FFmpeg's matrix/range arithmetic, rounding and especially 4:2:0 chroma filters are an independent reference, not proof of Chromium's internal conversion. Plane disagreement against that reference cannot automatically be labeled pure quantization. Prioritize 4:4:4, where spatial chroma resampling is absent; use controls to bound conversion differences before assigning a cause.
nextReadOnlyDiagnosticDesign.notAuthorizedByThisEvidence: No production edits, default-profile migration, bitrate-policy increase, shared dependency installation or threshold change.

gate.metric: interior RGB mean absolute error per frame versus the unchanged independent CPU oracle
decoders: Chromium VideoDecoder followed by sRGB OffscreenCanvas RGB readback

invariantControls: The original six 96x64 BGRA frames, source color metadata, noise, content, scene clock, timestamps, durations and original keyFrame flags are unchanged. No gate was relaxed.

The original short-codec baseline and full P0 variable-control case reproduce every original VP9 packet payload and all original FFmpeg-decoded RGB bytes, including after optional observation/error capture was added to the shared diagnostic helper.

Both variable controls omit bitrateMode just like the original input; capability results normalize this to variable. Quantizer cases change only bitrateMode and per-frame vp9.quantizer relative to their legal matched-profile controls.

The numeric bitrate field remains 56000 in every configuration. In quantizer mode this is not proof that bitrate control is still used. Every quantizer capability result retains bitrateMode:quantizer; actual configure and every successful encode call's submitted options are retained in the run artifacts.

IVF packets are independently checked with FFprobe SHA256 against the native encoder payloads. Every output has six frames, original dimensions and timing. Quantizer q0/q32/q63 produce distinct packets and decoded pixels for both profiles, establishing behavior beyond capability acceptance.
The seven diagnostic source hashes were frozen before the run and checked again after it. No Mediabunny callback mutation, production change, dependency update or installed-plugin operation was used.

configuration.quantizerEncodeOptionsDelta: Each original encode options object keeps keyFrame (true for the first frame, false for the other five) and adds vp9:{quantizer:q}. Values tested: 0,32,63.
configuration.observedMetadata: P0 is yuv420p and P1 is yuv444p. FFprobe and Chromium decoderConfig report smpte170m limited/tv range for both, despite the requested codec color fields.

conclusions: P0 q0, P1 q0 and P1 q32 pass all six original gates in both independent decoders on this fixture/runtime. This disproves a claim that this fixture's original gate is inherently unattainable with 4:2:0.
Increasing the fixed bitrate alone did not fix the previous experiment; an empirically effective per-frame quantizer control now provides a candidate integration path.

q0 is not RGB lossless: conversion/subsampling and other residuals remain. A passing tiny fixture does not establish a safe universal quantizer, size/performance budget, export preset or installed Electron acceptance.

The default production failure is not repaired by this standalone diagnostic. The earlier raw-YUV/no-codec design remains not run; this experiment does not fully separate conversion, chroma resampling and quantization residuals.

specifications.rangeCaution: The 2025 published Group Draft Note describes 0..63; the current Editor Draft describes 0..255. This diagnostic only uses their shared q0/q32/q63 values. A declaration is not runtime support or whole-pipeline losslessness evidence.

findings.finding: Native VideoEncoderBitrateMode includes quantizer; VideoEncoderEncodeOptions at line 3043 lacks vp9, while retaining avc/keyFrame. Missing TypeScript VP9 options do not establish a runtime limitation. A local structural option type is preferable to dependency mutation or any.

Mediabunny's public encoding bitrateMode admits only constant/variable; its runtime validator at line 297 rejects quantizer. The local CanvasSource constructor check accepted variable and rejected quantizer with that exact validator error.
Quality instances resolve to estimated numeric bitrates. Quality labels are not per-frame quantizer control.
Final per-frame options are assembled before onEncodedSample at line 484. Mutating sample options inside that observer is too late for this frame.
onEncoderConfig precedes native configure, but using mutation here to bypass Mediabunny validation is explicitly excluded from the proposed production approach.

Public EncodedVideoPacketSource('vp9') accepts EncodedPacket plus EncodedVideoChunkMetadata through add at line 204. Calls must preserve decode order while timestamps remain presentation timestamps; the returned promise is the mux/writer backpressure signal.

Public EncodedPacket.fromEncodedChunk(chunk) copies bytes and converts microsecond timestamps/durations to seconds. clone can supply precise original timing when required. Both classes are exported from the public package index.

proposedProductionAdapter.scope: A narrow native-WebCodecs browser platform adapter for explicitly requested VP9 quality control; keep existing rendering, audio, mux/output ownership, cancellation contract and compatible defaults. Product policy remains outside this diagnostic.
minimalFlow: Resolve an explicit, validated codec/profile and quantizer policy without inferring a global q default from this fixture. Probe the exact native VideoEncoderConfig, require quantizer mode to survive capability normalization, and report unsupported configuration without silently falling back.
Create a public EncodedVideoPacketSource('vp9') and connect it to the existing Output before starting. Do not patch Mediabunny or use private source/muxer members.

Own a native VideoEncoder configured with bitrateMode:'quantizer'. Construct each VideoFrame using the existing renderer's source, precise timestamp and duration; preserve the requested keyframe schedule and pass a local structurally typed vp9:{quantizer:q}. Always close owned frames.

In the native output callback, convert with EncodedPacket.fromEncodedChunk(chunk), preserve all actual decoder metadata, and enqueue packetSource.add(packet,metadata) in encoder emission/decode order. Restore precise original second-based timing via public packet.clone only when the mapping is unambiguous.

Bound both native encodeQueueSize and pending mux bytes/calls. The native output callback is not awaitable, so explicitly queue writes, propagate their first failure and await drain in the producer. Preserve audio/video interleaving rather than waiting in a way that deadlocks a muxer needing the other track.

On normal completion, await native encoder.flush, drain every queued packet write, close the packet source, then let the existing Output owner finalize only after all audio/video sources finish. Native flush alone does not mean mux writes are complete.

On cancellation/error, prevent late construction/output from reviving the session, close/reset the owned encoder as appropriate, settle queue waiters and reuse the existing exactly-once output cancel/finalize ownership. Never convert a partial artifact into a successful result.
acceptanceRequired: Keep the original six-frame CPU/native-input/original decoded-MAE acceptance unchanged; run through the real production export and decode the produced container with both independent decoders.
Verify actual configure/per-frame options, codec metadata, frame count, ordering, keyframes, duration, seeking and A/V sync in the final muxed artifact, not only raw IVF.

Regression-test default compatible exports and explicit unsupported mode rejection, runtime codec failure, mux rejection, first-frame cancellation, cancellation during capability/configure/flush, and late callbacks without leaking frames or finalizing twice.
Calibrate representative dimensions, frame rates, thin text, saturated graphics, grain, gradients and motion; measure size/performance before selecting public quality labels or any default quantizer.
Validate installed Electron separately: standalone Chromium 151 support is not proof of the application's Chromium runtime capabilities.
risks: Microseconds-to-seconds precision, duplicate rounded timestamps, missing chunk duration, reordered packets and midstream decoderConfig changes.
Native asynchronous callbacks, unawaitable output, bounded backpressure across both audio/video tracks and cancellation races.
Frame and encoded-packet ownership, memory amplification at low q, encoder speed and output size at real project scale.
VP9 profile/color metadata and browser/hardware differences; declared requested color fields are not proof of actual stream metadata.

The initial alpha:discard fixture does not cover alpha-preserving WebM. Do not silently drop an existing transparency requirement or claim this adapter supports alpha side data before implementing and testing it.
Published VP9 quantizer range 0..63 versus current editor-draft 0..255 discrepancy; tested common values are not justification to expand the public range.
excluded: claiming RGB-lossless output or full-song acceptance

quantizerFollowup.checkpointScope: Five diagnostic source files plus this evidence file only. Historical sourceFiles above refer to the prior matrix snapshot and remain unchanged.
